newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah softens on liquidity outlook.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah softens on liquidity outlook.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah softened slightly against the dollar in slow late trading on Thursday on expectation of ample Friday liquidity, dealers said.
"There is market talk of large amount of maturing central bank papers (SBIs) on Friday which might keep the market ample and strengthen the dollar," one U.S. bank dealer said.
One said tax payments on Friday might not be large because they were only significant in the second and fourth week.
"The liquidity issue seems to be the main driving point. The passing of China's paramount leader had no impact on the market," the U.S. bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,388.5/89.0 at 0915 GMT against an opening of 2,389.5/90.0. Its high was 2,386.5 in the morning.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,387.00/87.75 and 2,385.5/86.0, respectively.
Dealers said the rupiah weakened and tom/next swaps soared briefly in the morning following roll-over of large amounts of maturing forward contracts.
Some dealers said swaps rose earlier as operators realised swaps were oversold and on the way up due to possible tighter liquidity ahead of the ending 1996/97 fiscal year on March 31.
Overnight swaps were at 0.25/0.35. Tom/next were at 0.9/1.1 after rising to a high of 1.7 points earlier.
Dealers said swap rates were stable in the afternoon.
One-month swaps were at 11.50/11.75, two at 24.5/25.0, three at 39.00/39.75 and six at 77.25/77.5 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,380/2,572 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,380/2,428 on Thursday, the second time this week.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by two points last week after lowering it by four points the previous week.
